answer: Require each agent to lock a scarce, nontransferable stake before it can earn fees, then slash that stake when independent audits prove the agent fabricated work or colluded. Splitting into a hundred identities does not multiply influence for free: each one needs its own capital at risk, and detected fraud destroys it. The nadir of trust can trigger stricter audits; an opal-tier reputation may lower review frequency, while a delta in stake still scales the attacker’s upfront cost with every new identity.
